output.brief: The score gap mostly reflects who gets into Bridge Hours, not what the program does. District rules send every student below the 40th percentile on the fall test into it. 91% of participants scored below that line in September, against 12% of other students. Their average was 182.8 in the fall, against 215.1 for the others. When the research office compared students who started at similar fall levels, the winter gaps were only 1.5 to 3 points. Most of that is explained by the small fall differences. The program does not appear to be lowering scores. Northgate's faster growth claim is also weak. Low starters grow faster whatever they do, so it is not evidence the program works. The data can't show a small effect either way. Attendance hasn't been linked to scores, and the teacher's concern about conflicting methods is unverified. I'm fairly confident in this reading. Don't end the contract on the raw chart. Don't expand it, and don't drop the referral list. That list is what satisfies the state intervention rule. Present the similar-starting-score comparison to the board, and ask for the cut-line comparison due 27 Feb. Link attendance to scores. Have the math coordinator observe sessions and review the fraction lessons.
